skill.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
skill.description: Guides agents through resolving active Git merge or rebase conflicts by inspecting intent, resolving hunks, running checks, and completing the workflow.
skill.summary: Resolve active Git merge or rebase conflicts with source-backed decisions and project checks.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive caused by inline Markdown command text in SKILL.md. The skill is prompt-only guidance for Git merge and rebase conflict resolution, with no executable code, network access, secret handling, or prompt injection evidence found.

static_findings.snippet: 3. **Resolve each hunk.** Preserve both intents where possible. Where incompatible, pick the one mat

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 10 contains an inline Markdown mention of the git --abort option, not executable Ruby or shell code. The file is prompt-only guidance and does not invoke commands itself.

content.value_statement: Merge and rebase conflicts can hide lost intent and broken behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through source-backed conflict resolution and project checks.
actual_capabilities: Reviews the current merge or rebase state before editing conflicted files.
Uses commit messages, pull requests, issues, and tickets to understand intent.
Resolves each conflict hunk while preserving both changes where possible.
Chooses the change that matches the stated merge goal when intents conflict.
Finds and runs project checks such as typecheck, tests, and format.
Finishes the merge or rebase by staging changes and continuing the workflow.
limitations: It does not provide executable automation or custom merge tooling.
It needs repository history and project context to make strong decisions.
It cannot infer missing product intent when source evidence is unavailable.
It depends on the project exposing reliable checks and scripts.

use_cases.title: Finish a Feature Branch Merge
use_cases.description: Resolve conflicts while keeping the feature goal and main branch updates intact.

use_cases.title: Complete a Rebase Safely
use_cases.description: Work through each conflict during a rebase and continue only after checks pass.

use_cases.title: Review Conflict Decisions
use_cases.description: Explain why each hunk was resolved and document trade-offs for review.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect the Conflict State
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for understanding active conflicts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect my current Git merge or rebase conflict. Show the conflicted files, summarize the branches involved, and identify what context you need before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Specific File
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused help for one conflicted file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to resolve the conflict in [file path]. Check the surrounding code and relevant history, preserve both intents where possible, and explain each decision.

prompt_templates.title: Complete the Whole Merge
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to resolve all current conflicts. For each hunk, find the source intent, apply the safest resolution, run the project checks, fix merge-related failures, then stage the completed result.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Conflict Resolutions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit my completed conflict resolutions before I commit. Compare the resolved files against both sides of the conflict, identify any lost behavior, run relevant checks, and list remaining risks.

output_examples.input: A merge conflict exists in a service file after pulling main into a feature branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the conflict state, explains both versions, applies a resolution that keeps the feature and the main branch fix, then recommends typecheck and tests.

output_examples.input: A rebase stops on a conflict in a test file with incompatible assertions.
output_examples.output: The assistant traces the intent from recent commits, updates the assertions to match the rebased behavior, runs the relevant test command, and prepares the rebase to continue.

output_examples.input: A reviewer wants confidence that a resolved conflict did not drop behavior.
output_examples.output: The assistant compares the final file against both conflict sides, lists preserved behaviors, notes any trade-offs, and highlights checks that should pass before commit.

best_practices: Start by inspecting the merge or rebase state before editing files.
Use primary sources such as commits, pull requests, issues, and tickets.
Run typecheck, tests, and format after resolving conflicts.
anti_patterns: Do not resolve hunks by choosing one side without checking intent.
Do not invent new behavior to make conflicts disappear.
Do not finish the merge or rebase before project checks pass.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps resolve active Git merge and rebase conflicts with context, intent checks, and project validation.

faq.question: Does it run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives workflow guidance for an AI agent working in a repository.

faq.question: Can it handle rebase conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. The source instructions cover both merge and rebase conflict workflows.

faq.question: How does it choose between conflicting changes?
faq.answer: It preserves both intents when possible. If they are incompatible, it chooses the option that matches the merge goal.

faq.question: What checks should be run after resolving conflicts?
faq.answer: The skill recommends discovering project checks, usually typecheck, tests, and format.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: The source is prompt-only and contains no executable code. The audit found no semantic security issue.
